item.title: Beyond Consent
item.description: Russell Brand has been sentenced to ten years in prison for raping one woman and sexually assaulting three others. For his defence, Brand claimed that the encounters were all consensual even though he couldn’t remember them. ‘Consent is fundamental, essential, necessary,’ he told the court. Obvious as this should be, Brand’s past boasts imply that he saw consent not as a bare minimum, but as an obstacle to be overcome.

item.title: In Oujda
item.description: The office of the Moroccan Association for Aid to Migrants in Vulnerable Situations is arranged over two floors in a modest building in Oujda. The walls of one room are covered in pictures, including photographs of young men who have gone missing. There are also campaign posters calling for the abolition of the European Union’s border agency, Frontex.

item.title: The Philosophy of ‘To the Lighthouse’
item.description: In 1908, Virginia Woolf wrote that she hoped to revolutionise the novel and ‘capture multitudes of things at present fugitive’.To the Lighthouse(1927) marks perhaps her fullest realisation of the novel as philosophical enterprise, and not simply because one of its central characters is engaged with the problem of ‘subject and object and the nature of reality’.

item.title: Albert Camus: A Short Life
item.description: Albert Camus’s short life began in Algiers in 1913 and ended in a car crash near Paris in 1960. After being rejected from the École Normale because of a failed medical assessment, Camus became a journalist in Algiers and planned his writing career around three concepts based on the figures of Sisyphus, Prometheus and Nemesis, a scheme that he never finished.
